questions.question: Which of the following economic activities is categorized under primary economic activities?

options.text: Textile manufacturing and steel smelting
Agriculture, fishing, forestry, and mining
Banking, insurance, and wholesale trade
Scientific research and software engineering

questions.explanation: Primary economic activities focus directly on extracting or harvesting raw materials directly from the earth's natural environment. Examples include agriculture, fishing, forestry, and mining.

questions.question: What is Ethiopia's ranking in livestock (cattle) population in Africa and globally?

options.text: First in Africa and tenth in the world
Second in Africa and fifth in the world
Fifth in Africa and fifteenth in the world
Tenth in Africa and twentieth in the world

questions.explanation: Ethiopia possesses the largest livestock herd in Africa, holding 1st place on the continent and ranking 10th globally in total cattle population.

questions.question: Which river in Ethiopia is unique because it is the only river in the country navigable by water vessels?

options.text: Abbay River
Awash River
Baro River
Wabe Shebelle River

questions.explanation: The Baro River in Gambella is the only navigable river in Ethiopia because it flows over a gentle, flat lowland plain with sufficient water volume.

questions.question: Which agricultural commodity stands as Ethiopia's leading cash crop export, contributing roughly 28.6% of total national export earnings in 2019/20?

options.text: Oilseeds
Coffee
Chat
Pulses

questions.explanation: Coffee is Ethiopia's single most critical export commodity, accounting for approximately 28.6% of the country's total foreign exchange export earnings in 2019/20.
questions.sourceReference: Grade 9 Geography Textbook, Section 5.2, Page 133 & Section 5.3, Page 136 (Table 5.3)

questions.question: Which UNESCO World Heritage site in southern Ethiopia is famous for its extensive stone-walled dry terraces built for agricultural soil and water conservation?

options.text: Tiya Stelae
Fasil Ghebbi Castles
Axum Obelisks
Konso Cultural Landscape

questions.explanation: The Konso Cultural Landscape in southern Ethiopia was inscribed by UNESCO in 2011 as a cultural landscape featuring stone-walled terraces adapted for agricultural soil conservation over centuries.

questions.question: How do quinary economic activities differ from quaternary economic activities within the advanced service sector classification?

options.text: Quaternary activities involve manual labor in factories, whereas quinary activities involve subsistence farming.
Quaternary activities involve specialized knowledge and technical skill, whereas quinary activities involve high-level executive decision-making and policy formulation.
Quaternary activities are restricted to rural villages, whereas quinary activities take place at sea.
Quaternary activities generate agricultural commodities, whereas quinary activities process heavy metals.

questions.explanation: Quaternary activities focus on information processing, technical skills, and research, whereas quinary activities represent a subset of top-level decision-makers (government leaders, corporate executives, legal consultants) who shape policies and strategic directions.

questions.question: In which regions of Ethiopia is shifting cultivation (cut-and-burn farming) predominantly practiced?

options.text: Densely populated highlands of Shewa and Gojjam
Sparsely populated western lowlands such as Benishangul-Gumuz and Gambella
Urban municipalities along the Main Ethiopian Rift Valley
Cold Afroalpine peaks of the Bale and Semein mountains

questions.explanation: Shifting cultivation (cut-and-burn) requires low population density and ample forest cover. In Ethiopia, it is practiced along the western and southwestern lowland fringes like Benishangul-Gumuz and Gambella.

questions.question: Why does Ethiopia persistently experience a negative foreign trade balance (trade deficit)?

options.text: The value of domestic agricultural exports exceeds the cost of imported industrial goods.
The total annual value of merchandise imports consistently exceeds the total annual value of merchandise exports.
The government restricts all foreign currency exchanges for export items.
Service sector income completely offsets all physical commodity transactions.

questions.explanation: A trade deficit occurs when a nation's import expenditure exceeds its export earnings. Ethiopia imports costly capital goods, fuel, and consumer items while exporting mostly raw agricultural goods, resulting in a persistent negative trade balance.

questions.question: What historical factor contributed significantly to the slow technological transformation of traditional cottage industries (e.g., weaving, pottery, tanning, blacksmithing) in Ethiopia?

options.text: Complete absence of clay and iron ore deposits across the entire Ethiopian landmass.
Prevalent negative traditional social attitudes that marginalized artisans and assigned them low social status.
Government laws banning the local production of handwoven fabrics and pottery.
Overabundance of cheap imported industrial machinery during the 18th century.

questions.explanation: Historically, artisans engaged in traditional craft industries (potters, weavers, tanners, metalworkers) faced social prejudice and low social status, which hindered capital accumulation and technological innovation in cottage industries.

questions.question: Based on official distribution data for Ethiopian farm sizes (Table 5.2), what percentage of rural agricultural households operate on farm plots smaller than 1.0 hectare?
questions.explanation: According to Table 5.2, households with < 0.10 ha (7.71%), 0.10–0.5 ha (30.29%), and 0.51–1.00 ha (23.65%) sum up to 61.65% of all farming households in Ethiopia.

questions.question: According to road transport fleet records (Table 5.6), which administrative area accounts for over 55% of all registered vehicles in Ethiopia?

options.text: Addis Ababa City Administration
Oromia Region
Amhara Region
Sidama Region

questions.explanation: Addis Ababa City Administration accounted for 596,084 vehicles out of 1,071,345 total registered vehicles in Ethiopia (~55.6%), reflecting urban concentration in motor transport.

questions.question: Which major structural trend characterized the percentage contribution of economic sectors to Ethiopia's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) between 2014/15 and 2019/20 (Table 5.1)?

options.text: Agriculture increased its share from 32% to 60%, replacing services entirely.
The industrial sector dropped to under 5%, while agriculture became 80% of GDP.
Agriculture's GDP share gradually declined from 39.6% to 32.7%, while service (39.5%) and industry (29.0%) expanded their shares.
All three sectors maintained identical 33.3% equal shares across all six years.

questions.explanation: Table 5.1 shows that agriculture's share of GDP fell from 39.6% in 2014/15 to 32.7% in 2019/20, while the service sector emerged as the leading sector (39.5%) and industry expanded from 21.0% to 29.0%.

questions.question: Why does smallholder subsistence farming in Ethiopia remain exceptionally vulnerable to recurrent food insecurity during years with anomalous climate patterns?

options.text: Peasant farmers rely exclusively on heavy greenhouse drip irrigation that depletes groundwater.
Smallholder agriculture relies predominantly on rain-fed crop production using traditional hand tools, with minimal technological inputs and poor rural market infrastructure.
All agricultural soils in Ethiopia are composed of infertile Quaternary desert sand.
Export taxes force farmers to give 90% of their cereal harvest to foreign nations.

questions.explanation: Ethiopian smallholder agriculture relies overwhelmingly on natural rainfall and traditional tools (oxen-drawn ploughs, hand tools). Consequently, erratic or delayed rains cause immediate yield losses and household food insecurity.
questions.sourceReference: Grade 9 Geography Textbook, Section 5.2, Page 132 & Page 134

questions.question: How does the structural composition of Ethiopia's merchandise export trade compare to its merchandise import trade regarding processing levels?

options.text: Exports consist mainly of unprocessed primary agricultural items, whereas imports consist mainly of processed industrial capital goods, semi-finished items, and refined fuel.
Exports consist mainly of heavy electronic aircraft, whereas imports consist mainly of raw unrefined sugar.
Exports consist exclusively of refined petroleum, whereas imports consist exclusively of coffee beans.
Both exports and imports consist of identical proportions of raw timber.

questions.explanation: Ethiopia's export trade is dominated by raw or primary agricultural goods (coffee, oilseeds, pulses, chat, live animals), whereas import trade is dominated by high-value capital goods, machinery, semi-finished goods, consumer items, and fuel.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the specialized 'Pharma Wing' facility developed by Ethiopian Cargo and Logistics Services within the national air transport sector?

options.text: Manufacturing generic pharmaceutical tablets inside cargo airplanes during flight.
Providing specialized temperature-controlled cold-chain logistics for storing and distributing temperature-sensitive vaccines and medical supplies across Africa.
Training commercial pilots to perform surgical interventions in flight.
Exporting raw medical herbs exclusively to North American research centers.

questions.explanation: Ethiopian Cargo's 'Pharma Wing' is a state-of-the-art temperature-controlled cold-chain facility designed to store, handle, and transport temperature-sensitive pharmaceuticals and vaccines (e.g. COVID-19 vaccines) across global and African destinations.
